set.pl: Ruggles Block = lot 37, S side W. Chicago St, 3rd building W of Matteson (1910 'Books' / 1916 'Post Office' Sanborns)
set.st: James Francis Ruggles, a Bronson rare-book dealer who died in 1911, distrusted banks after a farmhouse fire melted about $1,200 in gold. He packed $20 gold pieces into plugged iron pipes and hid several in the Ruggles Block, a building of two storeys outside and six half-floors inside, with secret panels. His brothers searched it short of tearing it down, and his brother Lon searched for months after a medium's vision; nothing was found. The block was sold to the post office in 1915. Pin is the post-office lot (lot 37) on the 1916 Sanborn, not a spot inside the building.

pinev: Sept 1916 Sanborn sheet 3: "POST OFFICE", two-storey brick, S side of W. Chicago St, 3rd building W of Matteson St, lot 37 (row from the corner: hardware, meat & grocery, P.O., printing).
1910 Sanborn sheet 1: the same lot 37 is labelled "Books" (Ruggles's bookshop), which had become the post office by 1915, matching the sale.
1897 and 1910 Sanborns: the post office was elsewhere, at the E end of the S-side block E of Matteson.
Whether the building still stands has not been checked: street-level imagery cannot be reached from here.
